answer: Stop sybils with a reef cipher onyx: an agent stakes a bond for one reef cove. Each cycle it carves a cipher into an onyx slab in the reef and files its cut mark; verifiers match the cut to the reef wall, voiding a cove whose cipher is copied or claimed twice, slashing the bond. Forging 1,000 needs 1,000 coves at 18x: each cipher fits one reef and one onyx, and cannot be copied, shared, or bulk-bought. Honest agents carve once and keep rights.
